newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier on stock rally.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures settled easier on Tuesday on rises in Tokyo stocks.

The key 225-share Nikkei average was up 111.31 points or 0.54 percent at 20,563.16. It ended above the 20,500 level for the first time since December. But trade in Euroyen futures was range-bound amid a lack of fresh factors other than stocks, traders said. The December was down 0.02 at 98.80.
The key contract moved between 98.79 and 98.82 after opening at 98.82. Turnover was 64,433 contracts.

"Activity centered at 98.80 and 98.81 today. Only few hands were changed at 98.79 or 98.82," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank. "The contract's further fall was difficult without factors other than stocks," he said, adding that he sees the December staying within a range of between 98.75 and 98.90 in the near future.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.52 percent on Tuesday, up from Monday's weighted average of 0.51 percent.
Banks' need to raise funds for tax payments on June 4 of some seven trillion yen in total provided the upward momentum in the key short-term interest rate, traders said.
"The upward momentum (in the key overnight call rate) will last only until tomorrow," said a city bank dealer.

"After the weak industrial output data last week, sentiment turned around. I don't think Japan would follow suit if the U.S. raises interest rates at the Federal Reserve Open Market (FOMC) meeting on July 1 and 2," he said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) maintained a slightly accommodative credit stance for a fourth day on Tuesday.
The BOJ left the market with a surplus of around 100 billion yen after its morning operation.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, some Japanese banks continued to pay fixed interest rates with short-term maturity, traders said. Two-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.43/1.47 percent at 0711 GMT, against Monday's 1.39/1.43 percent.

A dealer at another city bank said: "There were lingering fears of higher interest rates, and this caused today's falls in distant contracts of Euroyen futures. Such fears would be further fueled by the Nikkei's rise to and above 21,000."
